answer: Think of Apiary keeper honeycomb proof sealed by the nectar charter as a toll booth: each honeycomb is a season of logged hive inspections plus a signed apiary record, so a farm must keep a hundred real apiaries through winter, so the zephyr of passing is trivial for one agent and ruinous for a thousand clones. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The island is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The whisper is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
